item.title: The Financial Sector | Seeking Critique first
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: Tale

Genre: Mystery

Elevator Pitch: My tale is about an accountant who monitors the budget of SCP containment procedures (especially Euclid SCPs). Euclid SCPs and Safe SCPs in this tale also have drastically reduced budgets to send more funding to Keter and other high priority SCPs (due to an incident that caused the foundation to receive a significant amount of less funding). However, when monitoring one SCP he notices large amounts of money seemingly going down the drain. After his concerns are dismissed by higher-ups, he decides to launch his own (unauthorized) investigation.

Central Narrative:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I decided on this idea for some perspective on what I
feel is like something that doesn't really get represented on the website (understandably so as it could limit containment procedures).

Additional Notes: I also would like to make this a tale series if I don't have enough space in the first tale

item.title: Anomalous-D
item.description: Not your ordinary lab rat.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch

Anomalous-D (AD) is an extradimensional parasite which feeds on the pain, fear, grief or rage of other sentient entities. It became entangled with our reality and assumed human form eventually finding its way into a Foundation D Class assignment after being captured and convicted of a string of sadistic crimes against animals and people. Its position as a D Class brings it into frequent close proximity of various other anomalies. Anomalous D devises novel ways provoke or torture these anomalies undetected so that it can feed off their pain and rage.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:

  • Containment procedure
  • Description of Entity
  • Description of how the creature came to be in containment / details of anomalous nature
  • Addenda:
    • Incident report: Containment breach first drawing scrutiny of AD
    • Memo: List of incident reports possibly involving AD
    • Interview: Log of the interview which reveals AD’s status as anomalous.
    • Interview: Log of feeding procedure
    • Memo: Detailing the variability of AD’s appearance
    • Memo: Possible reclassification as Keter / Thaumiel

Hook / Attention Grabber:

Following a major incident, the Foundation has confined it but is not sure that it is completely contained. Still, the possibility that this new anomaly may be used to injure or possibly destroy other anomalies is cannot be ignored.

Additional Notes:

Anomalous D typically resides between dimensions and might encounter various manifestations of other trans-dimensional creatures on its travels. It would not normally be able to feed on these entities as they would either be too powerful or impossible to hold on to. But in this reality it has found itself – quite accidentally – in a situation where the SCP foundation has trapped them and rendered them unable to defend themselves. Its motivation is to feed on their stress while not getting snared itself.

I expect that I’ll need lots of discussion and refinement to get this where I want it to be. This would be my first SCP contribution and I’m not an experienced writer. Additionally, most of what interests me in this concept are its possibilities for world-building and future story-telling. It will be challenging to bring this to life in a way that hooks the reader while also pointing to the other possibilities.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - Self-Casting Spell
item.description: An article about the people made out of thaumaturgy, who are also kinda Polish. For more, see inside.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A thaumaturgical sentient life-form, living deep in syberia, their culture with strong Polish influences left by Sybiraks. (Sybiraks were the Polish people resettled to Syberia.) It explores both the effects of Polish diaspora and the foundation containing a society.

Central Narrative: It starts off with the special containment procedures (the fenced off part of syberia), then there is a description (about how their bodies are made of what is basically sigils, about how they exchange spells that modify them as plasmids). Then it describes their culture, and the addeneum, where it is described how the sybiraks discover them and describe them, and offer them vodka and rabbit's blood, and how their societies get together, learning from each other and “forming a symbiosis”. It ends with the Incident, when they almost had a civil war.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The concept, I think. Also the ala genetics that arise inside them, and the weird stuff that arises cause of sentient beings being able to trade plasmids.

Additional Notes: Catholic sentient spells, which form tribes. An idea so weird, that it can work. Also their tribe is divided into three groups:
The Ultracatholics, lead by a Fanatical Pariah Priest, who want to make the other groups just as catholic.
The Tolerant, lead by the youngest of the elders, who want to cooperate with The Foundation, and to learn more of the outside world
The Traditionalists, lead by their shaman, who want to be freed and allowed to go back to the old Yakut ways.

item.title: Home is where I want to be
item.content:encoded:
Home, is where I want to be
But I guess I'm already there
I come home, she lifted up her wings
I guess that this must be the place


~David Byrne, "This Must Be the Place"

This tale is my attempt at emulating the style of Zyn's original Kiryu Labs series — probably one of the best early series on this site, propped up by Zyn's talent for writing heartwarming, touching stories with just the right balance between humour and heartfelt emotion. I hope I did Kiryu Labs justice with this.

Thanks to VoidLady, not_a_seagull, and Its a Bad Idea for helping me revise and edit this tale, and special thanks to Zyn for all that she does to help this community thrive. Have a wonderful New Year.

item.title: SCP-5365
item.content:encoded:
How do you write about an infectious disease in a global pandemic? Apparently you just have to make it cute!

I had a lot of fun writing this SCiP for Rigen for the holiday exchange! When I first got the prompt of making “art or tale about anomalous disease SCP/SCPs" I was really unsure of what to do since I couldn't figure out a way to do a tale about a disease without paralleling the current pandemic (and I honestly didn't realize that the request was for art or tale rather than an SCP until like 2 days before the due date). But I think what came out is fun and people have said it’s funny, cute, and really clever so I guess others agree! Happy Holidays everyone!

item.title: Dire Wolf
item.content:encoded:
This was my Art Exchange gift for Jacob Conwell, who asked for something that starred his character Sasha Merlo. I, however, hit a bit of a brick wall. Having read over a ton of Those Twisted Pines in preparation to write this character, I struggled because… she's finished! Her backstory is filled in by Kalinin, her frontstory is filled in by Jacob Conwell — and I mean, that covers her entire life. My first idea was to make a story centered around her husband, Gabe Merlo, but he's pretty developed as well, and has a boring job (no offense), so there wasn't much to do there either.

So I struggled a bit here, and then there, and bit my nails, was like oh no what do I do, until I realized that I had probably write a story about someone else in the canon while having Merlo be an important character in that story. As the tale evolved, Merlo's involvement went down until she had only two scenes (seen here), but… I couldn't figure out a better way to do it. So, Conwell, I'm sorry that this isn't precisely what you asked for, but I just fell in love with Phineas, and so here he is in all his glory.

Thanks for giving me such an interesting time. I've now read plenty more Twisted Pines than I'd ever read before, and my appreciation for your work has peaked. (Go check all your tales that feature Sasha Merlo. The majority of them have new comments by yours truly.)

There is more I want to say but it will have to wait until I have done some of my responsibilities for today.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Joke SCP - mind-influencing game code
item.description: A seemingly insignificant script which mysteriously appears
item.content:encoded:
A seemingly insignificant script which mysteriously appears in popular online multiplayers, generates a user account of which in game exposure can influence the mind.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Joke SCP

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: The SCP would be a few lines of code, which would transfer itself from one online multiplayer game to another.

Once the script is embedded within its host, it becomes uneditable or deletable, generating a fictitious user account, referred to as SCP-XXXX-1 (however the script contains not enough code to emulate a user account, leaving foundation staff puzzled).

SCP-XXXX-1 is always generated with an identical username (making identifying affected games an easier task). SCP-XXXX-1 spends a majority of its time in its "inactive" state. However, during short periodic "active" states it performs in game tasks, including text or voice communication (important to monitor for potential interviews and testing).

Any player (in game) to interact or be exposed to SCP-XXXX-1 would start developing symptoms of online addiction, anti-social behaviours and dysphoria.

Central Narrative: This article will be written according to the standard layout. Starting with containment procedures, a description and finishing with an addendum.

containment procedures will outline only monitorisation instructions for the host game ( including a cover-up story for participating publishing companies to grant the SCP foundation moderation privileges in addition to the games code). Players coming into "contact" with SCP-XXXX-1 are automatically added to foundation listings for interviews and eventual administration of amnestics. Because of its shifting nature, it is considered "not contained". However, due to SCP-XXXX-1's docile and collaborative personality, it has been classed as Euclid.

The description will detail the SCP's nature, it's odd properties and theories. In addition to, SCP-XXXX-1's description, behavioural patterns and anomalous effects on players and how to recover from the latter. Finally, ending with story of the SCP's discovery

The addendum will feature a list of games the SCP was previously part of.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This article seeks to create a fictitious origin for online additions to MMOs and becoming anti-social. In addition, this article is inspired by the collective input of the ChilloutVR community, by an inside joke/meme (hence "Joke SCP") of this very SCP joked to be the source of users who spend their lives in virtual reality (and by extension any other online multiplayers)

Additional Notes: I have a few concerns about copyright. Due to the nature of this article, it will rely heavily on existing games and companies to create the narrative. Am I allowed to use the names of existing companies?

As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. Also, please note the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit; your post is about 84 words over. Please address this before seeking further feedback. ~Zyn

item.title: The Lightswitch (Rewrite, seeking Greenlight)
item.description: An SCP is lost under questionable circumstances. [thread locked, repeat]
item.content:encoded:
An SCP is lost under questionable circumstances. An investigation begins to reveal lies within the Foundation.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Page Layout (Optional): Brief SCP article warning not to look into it (some sort of memetic hazard), most of the content being behind a high clearance level Addendum.

Elevator Pitch: A body-stealing lightswitch is handed around between various GOI’s that allows someone to forcibly take control of another.

Central Narrative: Created by a failed anartist, the UIU collected it from an anomalous smuggler trying to pawn over various low-level anomalies for a quick buck. The smuggler mysteriously vanished, and the UIU soon discovered it had the ability to allow people to enter the bodies of others (essentially controlling them and allowing access to their memories), and almost immediately it became a high priority target from the Foundation and other GOI’s.

+ show block
– hide block

After a series of raids, exchanges, purchases and various under-the-table dealings it finally lands in the Foundation's hands. It gets stolen once more (all too easily, its theft generates a lot of discontent with the Site Manager/containment directors complaining of higher up meddling), but the Foundation’s upper brass immediately demand they cease all investigation/pursuit attempts on it.

Soon after, the Foundation begins launching a series of extremely successful raids on other GOI’s, all ordered from the top brass only (with little communication to various MTF commanders/field directors). This isn’t unheard of (espionage naturally being confidential), but it does begin to grow concern of the lack of communication. A low level Researcher, Dr. Jonathan Moyer, looks more into the situation.

He starts pulling back layers and layers of lies, revealing that all the times the SCP hopped from GOI to GOI it was meticulously logged by the Foundation. He discovers that the UIU never actually discovered it, rather it was left on their doorstep one day. Turns out, the anartist who created it never existed, and at this point Dr. Moyer is closing in on the truth; all signs are pointing at the Foundation’s upper brass having far more influence than previously thought. As he starts following this trail to its end, he is suddenly killed during a containment breach of a seperate SCP he was working with. The top brass claim the breach was sabotage by the Chaos Insurgency, and refuse to allow anyone to look into it.

After this, the containment procedures are appended to include a (false) addendum mentioning an anti-memetic hazard, or some other nonsense to have people stop looking into it.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Explicit warnings not to look into it are up front, early on in the article. The warnings seem to have shaky reasoning to begin with.

item.title: SCP-3178
item.content:encoded:
The God you believe in is not only not good.
That God is cruel.

In 9th grade, I watched a documentary about the Russian Revolution, which ended on what was clearly meant to be a feel-good note with the Russian Orthodox Church canonizing Nicholas II. I'm thankful my ancestors, refugees from the Tsar's cruelty, weren't around to see such a thing.

Thanks to JackalRelated for SCP-5050, which heavily inspired the structure of this piece. Additionally, thanks to Ihp for helping me come up with the name for a nexus highway, and thanks to stormbreath and JackalRelated for the crit.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - The "Object"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: I do not have a complete page layout yet, however I would add in logs and addenda of stories and experiments involving encounters with this SCP in the main article.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-xxxx is an invisible object that cannot be detected by any kind of conventional scanning ray. Once at a location, it seeks out groups of 2+ individuals engaged in conversation. It will then proceed to take the form of whatever it is the speakers are presently discussing, including living creatures. When transformed into another object/being, the SCP will behave in a fashion consistent with the speakers' perception of the object/being. If uninterrupted by another transformation, the SCP's current transformation will last one hour before it goes back to its invisible state.

Central Narrative: SCP-xxxx was found in a hospital in 198x, following originally incredulous reports from the hospital's psychiatric ward. By the time it was captured by the SCP foundation it had indirectly caused 3 casualties and directly caused 1 casualty. Descriptions of the way the casualties came to be will be included. Witnesses at the hospital have been administered Class C amnestics.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: While there are other SCPs with the ability to transform (for example, SCP-2006), the "object" does not have a particular reason for doing so. It is "benign", because it does not seek to cause harm unless the speakers are discussing something dangerous. This way, there also is the possibility that a group of people could control it and gain great power; for example, the SCP could be helpful if it is made to transform into a tool or other instrument, but it could become scary if it is made to transform into a living murderer with a knife.

Additional Notes: I am thinking that perhaps the narrative should focus more on the breadth of incidents that can be caused by this anomaly rather than the casualties per se.

item.title: Adoption Poster: Scribbles!
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No, I already have pages up

Page Type: GoI Format

Elevator Pitch: The people who adopt Scribbles always seem to have magic-related issues. When his messages get decoded, they find out he was spying on them for an avian invasion all along.

Central Narrative: Scribbles the cedar waxwing can communicate by creating and arranging sticks on the ground into words. Nobody knows where the sticks he produces come from and he never creates sticks on camera. Because he can communicate, he chooses which people adopt him — all magic users from Three Portlands.

The first person who adopts him, Maria, observes that he keeps pecking lines into a certain stick, which he hides when he notices a human looking. When she comes home to find her magical protection system disabled with beak marks in its components, she returns him.

The second owner, Robert, notices that he's pecking dots and lines in a regular pattern, almost like words. He comes home one day to find ten waxwings attempting to peck through the door to his room full of magical books. Nine of them depart when he enters. Scribbles uses his sticks to ask to be taken back to Wilson's.

The third owner, Keith, grabs Scribbles' strangely pecked stick while Scribbles is engrossed in a magic book and sends it to his friend at Anderson Robotics who specializes in cryptography.

The decoded message shows that Scribbles has been spying on humans, planning an invasion of the city (and later humanity) with his group of waxwings. The stick records his observations and is meant to be passed onto other waxwings when the right moment arrives. He's been trying to access magical areas and study magic as a way of counteracting humans' strength and technology.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A cedar waxwing conspiracy sending a spy into Wilson's.

Additional Notes: I'm trying to decide whether this concept or my other Wilson's concept is better.

item.title: An uncommon network of tunnels
item.description: House of a space paradox and bizarre things
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Suspense and adventure (not sure what it may be)

Page Layout:
Containment procedures and description; followed by in-depth information, such as exploration logs, interviews, related documents or tests, which present events in a non-linear sequence. The page may use darker (in color) elements for ambiance sake (in regards to in-universe design and narrative support).
In-depth information may be organized in different parts with a ListPages module or any other medium for focusing.

Elevator Pitch:

► A mostly subterranean network of tunnels that has the following properties
▼ A mostly subterranean network of tunnels that has the following properties:
  • Inner distances (mainly the longitudinal extension) and shapes of some tunnels don't match those expected by outside measurements, especially in underground ones.
  • Various tunnels lead to impossible locations, such as the end of other tunnel, structures not existing outside the network or different realities.
  • It connects (not necessarily directly) to odd places of different nature and varying degrees of relation with each other.
  • It appears to be infinite in size and has entrances all around the world.
  • Network and attached rooms are occupied by diverse kinds of entities, items and information. They are not always hostile or sentient but inherently imply a risk.
  • Anomalous events occur within the complex; for example, reality-based, space-time and biological distortions.
  • Antimemetic and physical qualities affect the network so that all attempts to bring logic to the spatial paradox meet failure.

Central Narrative:
After the containment procedures and the description are told, the article will focus on the experiences around this SCP and the hidden history of the places "inside" it.

► This second part of the article will relate this information in the form of records
▼ This second part of the article will relate this information in the form of records,

for instance, the incidents lived and findings made by separate Foundation teams on exploration procedures, the speech of sapient beings inhabiting the tunnels, the unraveling of the stories of the facilities connected to the network; going from initial approaches upon discovery, up to how a guide-rope tied to an agent (who ventured into the tunnels) conducts to the corpse of the latter, despite she exited through the other end of a tunnel alive and tied to the guide-rope.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

► The "heart" of this concept is the in-depth data
▼ The "heart" of this concept is the in-depth data,

because of its significance for the article and how it is presented as a set of mysteries revolving around these places, which are features that, to my knowledge, are not prominent in the wiki.
All of this written as Foundation registries and excerpts from independent documents, having both clinical and literary tone. That is, the capacity of an informative text to not only tell data, but also narrate a story.

Additional Notes:
My major concerns are on the literary emphasis of the SCP, since I wouldn't like to create a tale made into an article. Keep in mind the concept is intended to form an actual SCP article, not a tale page designed as one.

item.title: The Bargainer
item.description: you can have it all, for the right price.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: a living humanoid mummy that can give you anything you want if you give it something it views as being equal in value.

Central Narrative: so far mostly just a series of tests on the SCPs abilities.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Bargainer is an advanced level reality warper with near omnipotent reality warping abilities, the only limits are that it can only use it's powers to keep up it's end of a bargain or protect itself. the SCP refuses to be given anything other than food for free, and will only accept personal belongings if it gives you something else in return. The Bargainer has a very primitive and basic understanding of monetary value, recognizing things like live humans, art, music, weapons, livestock, precious metals, and gems as been valuable, but doesn't understand the value of modern technologies, believing a sword that belonged to Genghis Khan is of equal value to a nuclear bomb. The SCP also lacks an understanding on how currency works, preferring to exchange things through barter. The Bargainer has a collection of personal belongings it has gained through trading with the foundation from tests, some of these items are; a sword from Genghis Khan, 20 beautiful maidens (20 conventionally attractive female personnel and D-Class who have never had sex), a David Bowie album, and a flock of chickens. The female personnel after living with the SCP for a month have mentioned that the SCP never attempted anything remotely sexual, and seems to just enjoy having company.

Additional Notes: I'm worried that the narrative I have right now isn't enough for this concept, but I'm not sure what else I could do narrative wise. The SCP avoids talking outside of bargains, due to how deteriorated it's throat is. I originally had this idea where the Bargainer had a deal with the Foundation that they would provide it with any worldly items it wanted within reason, and in return the bargainer would comply with Foundation commands, but that didn't feel like something the Foundation would be willing to agree to. Also felt like the limitations placed on it's abilities would help differentiate it from other reality warpers, what do you think?

item.title: SCP idea - (No name yet), Seeking Greenlights
item.description: An interesting and unique SCP. I am looking for critique and feedback.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: I will use the regular format. Information will be presented in the form of interviews with both the SCP and people under the SCP's effects, the unique procedures and descriptions of the SCP and it's many figurines as well as an audio log from the operation to capture the anomaly which was performed by an MTF unit. This log is what I will use to both explain how the foundation discovered it (repeated sightings of it's figurines) and serve as the start of the narrative for the article.

+ Elevator Pitch
- Title for hiding text

Elevator Pitch: It is a mechanical humanoid woman who has a large, rectangular hatch on her stomach. The SCP is indeed sentient however it does not act like it at all. It follows the exact same routine every day and night without need for sleep or nourishment, it is interested in absolutely nothing other than it's figurines and takes almost no notice of other creatures at all, choosing to entirely ignore them as if they did not exist. There have only been three instances ever in which it communicated with its research team, only two of which were able to be recorded.

Occasionally the hatch on it's stomach will open and a roughly head-sized block of wood will drop out. The SCP then takes it and sits down at a table to do what it does best, sculpt. It bites chunks into the wood block and slowly shapes it into a figurine of roughly 20cm height and 8cm width. Over time it will fully sculpt a figurine from the block, it's method of sculpting allowing it to ingest all the leftover material to form a new block in a fairly lengthy process. Most of the figurines it makes are very creepy and each is it's own sub-SCP. They each possess different and unique anomalous properties themed around different mental illnesses and can vary in danger from 'just stick it in a box' to keter level containment hazards. The main SCP continues this process of ejecting a block of wood and sculpting figurines with it until the whole block has been expended into the figurines at which point she consumes all her creations and starts the process again.

+ Central Narrative
- Title for hiding text

Central Narrative: As hinted at above, this SCP is themed around mental illnesses and what it would be like if they were to take a physical form. They are intended to be the embodiment of those health conditions with the figurines linked to the most common mental illnesses appearing most often. The narrative will start with an MTF log with the unit about to move in to capture the SCP so they can bring it back to the foundation. It will set up the figurines to all be entirely hostile and dangerous entities capable of catching MTF soldiers off-guard and killing them gruesomely. The way it will be structured will also be intended to make it seem like the main SCP is some mastermind puppeteer that is violent, threatening and in control of the figurines at all times just waiting for the moment to strike. Once it is captured and brought to a foundation site for study it quickly becomes clear to the research team that it is not actually a death machine and not all of the figurines it makes are dangerous weapons. What really catches everyone working of the SCP off guard is when one of the figurines that had been audibly crying and acting like it felt depressed successfully committed suicide. This event was so completely different when compared against all previous knowledge of the SCP that the research team launched an operation to document and discover as much about the behavior of the figurines as possible and lead to the discovery that the exact same ones could appear multiple times and all versions f the figurine would be identical. Before this it was just thought that the physical appearance and anomalous properties of the figurines was random and with no pattern. This lead to the creation of a specialized chart containing the details of all currently known figurines, how to identify them, what they all do and the special containment procedures for the figurines that require them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: First off I am not aware of any other robotic humanoids that eject a block of material from their body to sculpt small figurines out of so as far as I know it is very unique and different. Secondly I plan to create a wide variety of figurines that this SCP has made which will give people tons of brain candy and different situations involving different figurines to think about, also due to their large number there is likely to be at least one or two that everyone will find interesting to them.

Additional Notes: I could use some help coming up with a name for the main SCP. So far I've considered all the generic ones like Dollmaker, Sculptor, Sculptor's Handmaid, etc. but none of them are that good. If anyone has some more unorthodox ideas then don't be afraid to mention them.

item.title: SCP Concept: Guitar Hero
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX consists of two components, SCP-XXXX-1 which is a seemingly normal electric guitar and SCP-XXXX-2 which is an also seemingly normal amplifier. However, SCP-XXXX-2 has a unique connector only compatible with SCP-XXXX-1 that is unable to be unplugged on SCP-XXXX-2’s end. There is also no external power in the form of an electrical cable or battery compartment, but the power level seems to be associated with a colored light next to the connector port.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX-1 first appears to its victim at random. It appears to be an ordinary guitar, but when played it gives its victim talent far beyond their own, allowing them to play any song, chord, or note by simply thinking of it. In addition, SCP-XXXX-1’s strings release an endorphin-like substance referred to as SCP-XXXX-ɑ that, when absorbed through the victim’s fingers, releases a feeling of euphoria and an increased desire to use SCP-XXXX-1. If the person tries it, after several days SCP-XXXX-2 will appear in the same manner as SCP-XXXX-1.

+ show block
– hide block

If SCP-XXXX-1 is ignored, rather than SCP-XXXX-2 appearing, SCP-XXXX-1 will disappear before revealing itself to a new victim. If SCP-XXXX-1 is plugged into SCP-XXXX-2, SCP-XXXX-2 seems to enter an active state. After a seemingly random number of uses, SCP-XXXX-2 will suddenly attack the victim, striking them in the throat with its connector. It lodges into the throat below the vocal cords. SCP-XXXX-2 will then broadcast the inner thoughts of the victim. It will attempt to draw out thoughts that are embarrassing or hurtful, and will then feed off the negative emotions of the host. The light on SCP-XXXX-2 will gradually change from its current state to a bright green as it absorbs emotions, and when it has fully fed off the victim and is fully charged, the adapter will be removed and the victim left to bleed out as both objects teleport away to repeat the cycle. It is currently unknown where or how SCP-XXXX-2 uses stored energy and needs to recharge between victims. In extreme cases, the light flashes a deep red and SCP-XXXX-2 has been known to attack seemingly without activation by SCP-XXXX-1 in a desperate attempt to sustain itself. It is currently unknown what will happen if SCP-XXXX-2 is completely drained of power, and until containment procedures are considered adequate any experimentation on that subject has been banned by the Foundation for fear of any of SCP-XXXX's unknown anomalous effects.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP chooses victims based on interaction, and simply ignoring it is enough to spare oneself from falling victim to it. The Safe-class component of the object is used to attract and serve as bait for the Euclid-class portion of the SCP. It is capable of teleportation, and so containment proves difficult as someone, usually D-class personnel, must routinely interact with SCP-XXXX-1 which will inherently draw SCP-XXXX-2 to it, but the two must never be allowed to be used together. When SCP-XXXX-2 appears in SCP-XXXX-1's containment chamber, any personnel in the room are to be immediately evacuated and anyone who had contact with SCP-XXXX-1 is to be put into quarantine while a containment team returns SCP-XXXX-2 to its original containment.

Additional Notes:

n/a

item.title: Seeking greenlight: Merit to Match
item.description: A bit of anomalous propaganda designed to make its own premise true
item.content:encoded:
A bit of anomalous propaganda designed to make its own premise true: that people deserve where they end up in life.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror (?)

Elevator Pitch: A series of memetic ads/posts, detailing a philosophy about how to earn money and live a successful life (think the garage Lamborghini guy). The contained meme alters the personality of people exposed to it so that they deserve whatever they currently have (rich people become smart and diligent, poor people become delinquent and irresponsible, convicted people become violent and unstable, etc.). It is revealed to be funded by an anomalous entrepreneur with a message.

Central Narrative:

The Object Class is Neutralized, with a footnote explaining that non-anomalous lasting effects are still ongoing. The Foundation has already wiped the anomaly off the internet, and is investigating the PoI behind the anomaly. Nothing else can be done.

+ show block
– hide block

The description details the anomalous campaign's presence on social media and some of the text/videos it included. The memetic effects apply to anyone who watches one of the videos uninterrupted start to end. This alters their personality based on their present circumstances. (But the reveal of how comes later)

Discovery: The Foundation only discovers the anomalous properties of the ad campaign after it has existed for a few weeks and already gone moderately viral. It is discovered when a few Foundation researchers who watched the videos start performing noticeably better.

Tests are run on D-class, who don't seemingly experience any positive effects after exposure. Given its' beneficial effects on Level 1+ staff, the Foundation approves its experimental use on more researchers. In the weeks afterwards, the exposed D-class are discovered to be more hostile. One of them kills another D-class.

Conversation Log: The Foundation calls the maker of the campaign using a phone number in the ads and has a discussion with them. After the PoI realizes the Foundation is calling, they explain that the ad campaign is meant to promote "Justice" by creating a world in which more people deserve what they have, and more anecdotal evidence exists that peoples' character determines the circumstances where they end up. They promise they'll make more anomalies in the future and hang up.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The immediate hook is the Neutralized object class with the caveat attached, making the reader wonder what kind of damage has been done. For the first half of the article, the reader assumes the anomaly is "a self help ad campaign that makes people better", and then the actual nature of the anomaly comes as a twist/gut-punch.

item.title: SCP-XXXX "The Frozen Wood"
item.description: A snowy, unassuming forest, unable to support life of any kind... Except it's own...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article, Tale (after SCP is established)

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional

Class: Euclid

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX is a snowy, Birch forest varying in size, but often appears in a 10 KM x 12 KM radius. The subject seems to teleport to areas around the world at random (along with anything inside it), leaving a large, empty area in its wake, but is limited to cold climates and places that are experiencing severe winter storms. Strangely, the area always seems to be entirely sterile, no life can survive, be it plant, animal, bacteria, or even tardigrade!

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

The SCP tale I was planning for this follows a lone huntsman as he has unknowingly stumbled into this forest looking for game. He starts feeling weak, his vision blurry, and the snow taking on a slight red-ish hue. He starts coughing up blood, eventually too weak to go any further and contemplates his own mortality as he slowly dies in the snow. A lot of this story will have to do with what goes on in the character's mind, and how he deals with his impending death. (just a summary of the story)

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ show block
– hide block

As stated before, the forest cannot support any life whatsoever, except for the trees that grow in it; these trees, designated SCP-XXXX-A, release a toxic, spore-like pollen that sterilizes and kills all known terrestrial lifeforms (many SCP's are not affected), but thankfully, only within it's area of effect. These spores are inhaled and break down the cells of the organism, causing: internal bleeding from torn organ tissue, destruction of muscle fibers/tissue leading to paralysis, vomiting blood, asphyxiation, convulsions and/or seizures, etc., always ending with total organ failure and death.

After tracking it for years and sending hazmat-suit equipped recovery teams into the area, a total of 247 human bodies have been discovered, as well as the corpses of wildlife native to many different regions. Strangely, these bodies were perfectly intact, no decay had occurred as there were no bacteria left to break the bodies down.

Additional Notes:

- The spores from SCP-XXXX-A cannot survive outside of SCP-XXXX's area of effect, thus, the only way to study the spores is to be within the subject itself.

- Due to its often secluded location and it's deadly nature, as long as the Foundation is careful about the spores, a well protected base could be built inside the area as well as utilizing its random teleportation effect to avoid detection by the public!

item.content:encoded:
I found this ending from this video.

So, after you enter EZ and start searching for Gate-B and avoiding MTFs, after you finally enter the elevator. This happens:
SCP-173 enters and then snaps your neck and the game ends.

This is the dialogue that you can hear after that happens.

"Sir, there's a Class-D outside the elevator in Gate-B. Should we send someone in to get him?

"He might have some useful information about what's going on in there. I'll call-

"Never mind sir. It looks like 173 already took care of him.

Dialog end.

Unfortunately, since the ending is deleted, you can only get this through commands. If you want to test this out, here is the command. The command is:
ending b1

Hope it works for you! :)

item.title: SCP-XXXX - The Division Bell
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror/History

Elevator Pitch: An archaic bell that when rung instils extreme feelings of revulsion and loathing towards other humans (to the point of violence)

Central Narrative:
Discovery log - This will describe the findings of the archaeological dig where the bell was found. Summarised:
Discovered in the Fens near Crowland Abbey, England.
Surrounded by human skeletal remains bearing signs of violence (broken bones, crushed skulls, incision marks, burn marks, etc.
Dated to circa 710 CE.
Unusual bronze composition (higher than normal tin percentage; presence of antimony - unknown at time bell casting)
Inscription on bell 'belli munus' (Latin for 'gift of war')
Essentially, the discovery log will hint at something unusual, setting the stage for the incident log, where the anomalous properties were discovered.

Incident log - This will describe what happened when a historical society/museum renovated it and rang it for the first time: all attendees consumed with revulsion and/or loathing, leading to much violence including deaths and serious injuries. Probably a description from security and/or news camera footage at the venue.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Addendum 1 - this will link the bell to Guthlac of Crowland - an ascetic hermit monk who later had an abbey built for him by the king of Mercia, and was said to be plagued by demons (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guthlac_of_Crowland). The implication will be that the demons made him create the bell during his isolation.
Addendum 2 - this will briefly describe some lost notes from the Hemony brothers (real world bell founders from the 1600s), with a design identical to the Fens bell - plus documentation that several of these were manufactured and sold (to unknown parties). And possibly notes for an 'improved' design.

Additional Notes:
I'd like to have a sound clip of the bell to either play automatically a certain amount of time after opening the article (creepy but not really within the SCP format) or after clicking one/many links with appropriate warnings/security credentials ('Confirm level 3 access', 'Confirm you are alone', 'Confirm you are shackled' etc.).


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Lost objects appear at 0°N 0°E (Greenlight)
item.description: Teleportation/time travel tests to unset coordinates cause major explosions when objects overlap.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Anomaly

Page Layout (Optional): Description, table of recovered instances, discovery, addendum with notable events, appendixes with anticipated future events and recommendations.

Elevator Pitch: Objects randomly appear at exactly 0°N 0°E presumably due to teleportation to unset coordinates. The objects intersect with whatever is already there in the ocean in high-energy mergers. Similarly time travel mistakes happen where many objects appear simultaneously at times such the Unix epoch (1970-01-01) and the GPS epoch (1980-01-06) resulting in very large explosions.

Central Narrative: A very large explosion happens at 0°N 0°E on 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC. The Foundation discovers objects randomly appearing there, almost always destroyed by the high-energy intersection with what's already there in the ocean. The objects vary from junk to high tech equipment potentially from the future, accidentally sent to unset coordinates. Further explosions happen during the GPS epochs on 1980-01-01, and 1999-08-21, and the Foundation figures out the computing aspect. The Y2K bug confirms it and the Foundation anticipates further events and mitigates them. It turns out time overflow bugs also caused major explosions back in 1900 and 1901 and more are due in 2036 and 2038. The Foundation recommends switching to better time keeping formats.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Specific containment procedures to stay away from 0°N 0°E (Null Island) with hints of dangerous events that nuclear nations needs to be informed about, a picture of an flaming object manifesting in the ocena.

Additional Notes: I already wrote a complete draft at http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/sortie but need to go through the greenlight policy as a first time author.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlights and tips!) Portraitly.ai
item.description: A neural network begins whirring out brand-new and completely unique humanoid entities.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror/Sci-Fi

Elevator Pitch:
+Show Elevator Pitch
-Hide Elevator Pitch

An indie neural network project with the purpose of generating human portraits through combining several photographs of different people begins to manifest entities that appear to perfectly match the human shown in the image, except for the absence of any body parts not shown in the image. However, the entities are still able to propel themselves by unknown means. These entities vocalize through a combination of word jumbles composed of both English and French and through EDM bass drop samples. The humanoid entities prove difficult to terminate, as they are able to demanifest their physical form through a crouching motion.

Central Narrative:
+Show Central Narrative
-Hide Central Narrative

SCP-XXXX was first made known to the foundation after a series of reports detailing the sudden manifestation of a disembodied male head outside of the Arvonne Fraser Library in Minneapolis, Minnesota to local authorities. The Minneapolis Police Department passed the reports to the SCP Foundation, which immediately detained the entity and administered amnestics to witnesses of the event as well as propagating an online disinformation campaign, as images of the entity were posted on multiple websites. The entity was then interviewed by the site-19 researcher, Dr. Sharpe. The interview was conducted with the objective of discerning any potential information about the entity that it may be able to convey. Dr. Sharpe ascertained that the entity is capable of simple communication through the use of word association games. During these games, the entity mentions the word "Portraitly" which, after further research into the initial SCP-XXXX event, matched computer browsing history logs from inside the library. The interview was terminated after Dr. Sharpe apparently pointed out a patch of acne under the entity's hairline, which caused the entity to cease cooperation with Dr. Sharpe. The entity is contained in a standard humanoid chamber. Testing of SCP-XXXX determined that Portraitly.ai, a website hosting an anomalous neural network, manifests a seemingly random entity in the area of any subject using the website. Pressing the "Reload" option on Portraitly.ai prompts the website to generate a new image, which in turn manifests a new entity.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
+Show Hook
-Hide Hook

I haven't seen many SCP articles covering neural network sites, so I think it may be interesting to write about one possibly going wrong, especially with the rise of deep fakes and image generators.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP pitch, so any critique, greenlights, or, advice would be greatly appreciated!

Hook/Attention-Grabber: upon observation of a deceased victim of SCP-XXXX they find that the noes overtakes a person, turning skin into that of a cheap Halloween mask rubber, their cloths had been effected as well being overtaken by light fabrics like a cheap costume binding to not only frantic but the skin as well much like it was stitching together

Additional Notes: each face is unique and terrifying, no instant of this SCP has taken a life, but all instances have perished either due to fearful reactions of bystanders shooting in self defense, or long term starvation due to the fact an infected individuals loses the will and ability to eat or drink, more research to be conducted.

item.title: A Wholesome Gift
item.description: A gift, of some sort.
item.content:encoded:
Sandbox link, clocking in at around 2k words.

+ Spoilers?
- Close

The main plot follows the story of Xasbo, a guy who adores cats, until at one of the festivals, he unknowingly consumes his own cat in part due to a tradition in some parts of China which practise the culture of eating cat meat, leading to his disillusionment. The practice itself isn't widely practised, and it's more centered within the Guangdong and Guangxi provinces, so the latter was the first pick of where the massacre happened. After the villagers die, the place somehow got the anomalous power to serve as a place for housing cats.

You can probably say he's more of the extreme of the extreme, PETA activist who cares nothing for humankind.

Main concerns are SPaG, whether the interview is a huge exposition dump, whether Xasbo's personality can mirror more of a subtly psychopathic character, and whether it ends on a sufficiently spooky note in contrast to Xasbo's view of a literal massacre as a festive occasion for the cats.

item.title: The Flight of the Koalas
item.description: A tale about the emergency evacuation of koalas using flying serpents.
item.content:encoded:
Word Count: 2,371

Link: http://scpdsandbox.wikidot.com/veraltanic-page-3-0

Hello everyone! This is Veralta once again completing a draft that I hope to publish as a New Year's gift! I have written a social commentary about koalas, how they and the aboriginal Australians have been affected by the bushland fires, and how people should be more ecologically-minded. I also featured a trip throughout Australia's rich culture and locations, with several of the article's parts being based on Dreamtime1 lore.

Note: I have tried to make the parts of the article that I have based on Dreamtime to be as least abstract as possible, and clear. If there are questions or ambiguity that you can find about them, feel free to mention it in the critique!

Here are the points that I want to be reviewed:

1. Is the pacing and narrative good enough?
2. Is the worldbuilding and attention to detail decent and palatable?
3. Does it sound too preachy?
4. If applicable, have you noticed several problems and contradictions with Dreamtime lore and aboriginal beliefs?2

All in all, I hope you enjoy this SCP in time for the New Year (and a new leaf for all of us)! Thank you to those who will review this!

Footnotes
1. Umbrella term for aboriginal Australian beliefs.
2. I have researched this part as much as possible, so I would like to not screw up something here.
